Class DefaultJournal<T>

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.substrate.core.journal.DefaultJournal<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of value appended to this journal
All Implemented Interfaces:
Journal<T>
public class DefaultJournal<T> extends Object implements Journal<T>
Default Journal handle: an append-only sequence at a key, read forward from a cursor and closed by completing it.

  • Method Details

    • append

      public String append(T data, Duration ttl)
      Description copied from interface: Journal
      Appends an entry to this journal with the given time-to-live.

      Each successful append resets the journal's inactivity timer.

      The entry TTL is a per-record retention hint rather than a lease, so Duration.ZERO is legal and means "store this entry without a TTL". Backends that manage retention at the stream level rather than per entry ignore the value entirely.

      Specified by:
      append in interface Journal<T>
      Parameters:
      data - the entry payload
      ttl - time-to-live for this individual entry, or Duration.ZERO for no TTL
      Returns:
      the generated entry ID, monotonically ordered with respect to other entries in this journal

    • complete

      public void complete(Duration retentionTtl)
      Description copied from interface: Journal
      Marks this journal as completed with the given retention TTL.

      After completion no further entries may be appended. Existing entries and active subscriptions remain readable until the retention period elapses, at which point the journal expires fully.

      Like the entry TTL, the retention TTL is a retention hint rather than a lease: Duration.ZERO is legal and means "retain without a TTL".

      Specified by:
      complete in interface Journal<T>
      Parameters:
      retentionTtl - how long the journal remains readable after completion, or Duration.ZERO for no TTL

      public BlockingSubscription<JournalEntry<T>> subscribe()
      Description copied from interface: Journal
      Subscribe from the current tail. Only entries appended after this call are delivered. Historical entries (those already in the journal when subscribe is called) are NOT replayed.
      Specified by:
      subscribe in interface Journal<T>
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription that delivers future entries

    • subscribeAfter

      public BlockingSubscription<JournalEntry<T>> subscribeAfter(String afterId)
      Description copied from interface: Journal
      Subscribe starting strictly after afterId. All entries with an id greater than afterId are delivered, followed by new entries as they arrive. Useful for resuming from a persisted checkpoint.
      Specified by:
      subscribeAfter in interface Journal<T>
      Parameters:
      afterId - the entry ID to resume after (exclusive)
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription starting after the given entry
